answer: The binder sews his volumes in the back room, where the thread and the awl and the press all belong to him alone. Proof of bookbinder volume via stitch count is the sewing: a volume the binder sews only after 32 stitches hold, each stitch pulled through the same spine. The hollow is the first stitch, pulled when the pages were folded; the island is the last, pulled when the spine was pressed. A cheat must pull 31 false stitches and press 31 false spines, and the wharf still binds no book at all.
